newsitem.title: TURKEY: Yilmaz to meet rival in Turkish coalition talks.
newsitem.headline: Yilmaz to meet rival in Turkish coalition talks.

text.p: Turkey's two rival conservative leaders were to meet on Tuesday in an attempt to forge a secularist alliance despite a bitter personal feud that boosts the flagging Islamists.
Prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz and Tansu Ciller, the caretaker foreign minister, were set to hold talks in parliament at 1100 GMT on setting up a new coalition, party officials said.
But the chances of agreement appeared slim after Ciller's True Path Party (DYP) rejected an offer to share power from Yilmaz on Monday.
Investors in Istanbul came back down to earth following a buying spree on Monday fuelled by hopes that Yilmaz was on course to form a new government.

The morning session closed down 3.49 points. "The market was irritated by the possibility that the conservative True Path Party may not support the new alliance," said Okan Gulek from Taksim Securities. Shares had soared eight percent on Monday.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, an Islamist, resigned last week after frequent disputes with the army over religious activism.
He backs a pro-Islamist alliance headed by Ciller, who has served as Erbakan's coalition partner for the last year.
Ciller was in the the running to head a new government but President Suleyman Demirel snubbed her last week by asking Yilmaz to draw up a cabinet list.

A leftist leader said he would support Yilmaz's secularist grouping, although it is still around a dozen votes short of the simple majority needed to win a confidence vote in the 550-member parliament.
"We are in favour of giving a vote of confidence to the new government," leader Deniz Baykal told a meeting of his Republican People's Party deputies.
The Turkish press says Yilmaz is trying to woo True Path members into his proposed alliance at the expense of Ciller.
